- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is trending down, model often underestimates true price rise — correct by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (true > 70), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3) and forecast is flat or slightly rising, model often underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if 18-day history shows volatility, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 7–10 days to account for mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often fails to capture short-term volatility — increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.7% for next 5–7 days to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
